name: The Treasury
summary: Bronze by the ingot, gold by the face: the wanax's wealth, stacked and shelved in a plain red-footed room.
description: Here is where a king keeps the things that make him one. Oxhide ingots lie in crosswise stacks on their pallets like loaves in a bakery nobody is allowed to eat from, faience figures crowd a shelf in the corner, and on a stepped plinth of gypsum the gold death-mask of some earlier king looks out at the door with an expression of permanent disappointment. The room is plain on purpose: no frescoes, only a red dado, because nobody comes here to look at the walls. Everything in it is loot, and most of it is heavy.
build: Shell: the kit's Keep shell, 12.0 × 12.0 × 0.30 m slab, 0.50 m ochre plaster walls 4.60 m clear, 0.45 m haematite capstone band, an archway 2.60 × 3.31 m centred on every wall.
Dado: a haematite panel 0.40 m tall at the foot of every wall section (4.10 m wide, centred ±3.40 along each wall), flat against the wall.
Death-mask plinth (NE): gypsum block 1.40 × 1.40 × 0.50 m centred (4.30, 4.30), a second block 0.80 × 0.80 × 0.40 m on top (top at 1.20 m above ground).
Gold death-mask: an oval 0.28 wide × 0.13 deep × 0.39 m tall, standing on the upper plinth at (4.30, 4.30).
Ingot stack SE: a timber pallet 1.80 × 1.20 × 0.12 m at (4.00, −4.30), four crosswise layers of oxhide ingots 0.56 × 0.36 × 0.06 m (alternate layers 0.52 × 0.40), 2 × 2 per layer; top at 0.66 m.
Ingot stack SW: a pallet 1.20 × 0.90 × 0.12 m at (−3.90, −2.90), three layers, 1 × 2 per layer; top at 0.60 m.
Chests: two cypress chests 1.00 × 0.60 × 0.55 m with bronze-bound lids 0.05 m, against the south wall at x −4.60 and −2.90, y −4.90.

Faience shelf (NW): a timber shelf unit 3.00 m wide × 0.45 m deep, three boards at 0.35, 0.90 and 1.45 m above the floor, backed against the north wall at x −3.70, y 5.20; small faience flasks (0.26 m tall, 0.16 m belly) on every board.
Tripods: two bronze tripods, legs 0.90 m, bowl r 0.30 m, at (−2.40, 2.60) and (2.60, 4.60), the second standing guard by the plinth.
Cauldrons (SE): two bronze cauldrons r 0.34 → 0.26 m × 0.45 m on the floor at (4.20, −2.30) and (5.00, −2.30), soot inside.
Everything stands in the corner quadrants; the clear cross between the archways is bare floor.
sockets: Archway ×4, centred on each wall: 2.60 × 3.31 m (Keep), all open
Death-mask plinth: NE, the room's prize at 1.20 m

loot_anchors.at: east tripod bowl, by the plinth

materials.name: Ochre plaster
materials.notes: Walls; chalky, soot only faintly at the top (no hearth here).

materials.name: Haematite red
materials.notes: Dado and capstone band; scuffed pale at knee height by the stacks.

materials.name: Cast bronze
materials.notes: Ingots, tripods, cauldrons, chest bindings; ingot edges bright, faces dull and pitted.

materials.name: Faience
materials.notes: Flasks and figures on the shelf; glossy, crazed.

materials.name: Gypsum
materials.notes: The stepped plinth; worn at the front edge.

materials.name: Gold
materials.notes: The death-mask only: it is the loot.

gameplay: Ten loot anchors, most of them heavy: an ingot stack is several trips or a two-player carry.
The death-mask is the room's prize and sits in plain sight of the north and east archways.
No hearth and no frescoes: the room is dim, lit only from the doorways, so it is a good place to hide and a bad place to be found.
The ingot stacks are low cover (0.60–0.66 m); the plinth and shelf are the only tall cover.
